evidence.C1: Key-press runs on this build: 9 of 10 finished... the tenth hit a pedestrian... and was arrested
evidence.C2: Player character is a simple block (Screenshot 7) while cars and buildings have detailed textures and lighting
evidence.C3: Perks... tie the side activities together... jobs, police, money sinks and secrets that feed each other
evidence.C4: Key binding 'R: Restart / handbrake' creates ambiguity between driving mechanics and resetting progress
evidence.C5: Section 'Not covered by the tests' plainly states limits like 'No real players have tried it yet'

fixes: Implement a 'tutorial shield' that prevents police arrests during the first story job to guarantee the sub-60s onboarding flow for all players.
Upgrade the player character model to match the fidelity of the vehicles and environment, reducing the tonal clash between the blocky avatar and the detailed city.
Disambiguate the 'R' key binding (currently 'Restart / handbrake') to prevent accidental job resets while driving or confusion in control schemes.

evidence.C1: Title screen shows six keys and 'New Game'; first objective 'Get into the red car ahead [F]' is clear; first job cut to under a minute ending at Sol Wheel pier; learner car rule prevents burning-car ending; minimap and road arrows guide the route. However, 1 of 10 key-press runs still ended in BUSTED from a pedestrian collision, and the title screen carries settings, controls, 'what changed' line and disclaimer simultaneously.
evidence.C2: Four districts with distinct palettes (Meridian aqua/coral/cream/lilac, Rustport rust/ochre/sea-green, Sol Beach pastel), 86 painted walls with district-specific designs, day/night cycle with lit windows and neon trim, Coastliner airship, Sol Wheel, parasols and gulls. Screenshots show recognisable mood (sunset beach, neon night street, painted RUSTPORT wall). Graphics remain low-poly and the city reads as a sandbox rather than a place with deep atmosphere.
evidence.C3: Six story jobs ($250-$3,500), four odd-job types (Rush Order, Repo Run, Block Dash, Hot Parcel), cab fares with tip/streak math, four buyable properties with rent, 15 hidden packages, harbor courier shift, Sol Wheel ride, perks that tie activities together (5 packages = 25% less damage, 10 fares = double tips, all jobs = +50% rent), and money sinks (respray, repair, ammo, hospital, bail, three-stage tune-up). Activities clearly feed each other.
evidence.C4: HUD reduced to cash and health; stars appear only when wanted; weapon line shows for 5s after change or on low ammo; clock moved to map and pause screens; pause screen is three buttons plus settings and perks; map legend integrated onto the big map; G8 passed at three resolutions. Screenshots show clean layout with cash top-right, health bar, minimap bottom-left, speed and car condition bottom-centre, objective top-centre.
evidence.C5: Own city, names and art; G9 own-names gate passed; title screen carries 'An original open city sandbox in one file... not affiliated with the publisher or the series it is often compared to'; 'Not covered by the tests' section plainly states driving feel, synth radio, real-input coverage (only one job driven by key presses), single-platform testing, and 'No real players have tried it yet'.

fixes: Make the first job truly unwinnable-to-lose: the learner-car rule prevents a burning car but 1/10 scripted runs still ended in BUSTED from a pedestrian hit, so extend the protection to suppress arrests (or wanted level) until the first job beam is reached.

Add real-input test coverage beyond the single first job — five of six story jobs, all cab fares and the courier shift are only script-driven, so their time limits and difficulty are unmeasured and likely unbalanced for a human player.

Reduce title-screen information density: settings, six keys, 'what changed' line and the not-affiliated disclaimer all show at once; fold settings and the release history behind one button so the first screen reads as 'New Game / Harbor courier shift / Controls'.

evidence.C1: Title 'shows six keys', first view prompts 'Get into the red car ahead [F]', learner car 'cannot be wrecked'; but 'the tenth hit a pedestrian 25 m short... was arrested by a patrol car that was passing' - 1 in 10 first minutes ends in BUSTED through no fault of the player
evidence.C2: Dusk Sol Wheel shot, '86 painted walls', night where 'every car throws a pool of light' are strong; but the day Meridian screenshot reads as plain grey-blue blocks, so 'recognisable from one screenshot' holds only for dusk/night
evidence.C3: 'Six story jobs', four odd-job kinds, cab fares, property, packages, and 'Perks... tie the side activities together'; heat gates cab/tune-up/wheel. Docked because 'their difficulty and their time limits are not measured' for most activities
evidence.C4: 'the HUD is cash and health; the stars appear only when you are wanted', G8 'no overlaps at 3 sizes'; but the pause/map screens keep the driving HUD (minimap, speed, objective banner) visible beneath the overlay, and the perk card adds a text block under cash
evidence.C5: 'Own city, names and art', plain limits: 'No real players have tried it yet', only one job key-press tested; docked one point as the 'BUSTED' banner and 1-5 wanted stars mirror the disclaimed series' signature presentation

fixes: Make the first job arrest-proof (no patrol spawns or a stars-grace on the first-job route) so 10 of 10 key-press runs finish; the reported random BUSTED 25 m short is the last real first-minute failure on the highest-weighted criterion
Give the daytime city the same instant identity as dusk/night - stronger district colour and landmark silhouettes at distance, since the day Meridian view still reads as generic grey blocks
Extend key-press testing (test/drive.py style) to the remaining jobs, cab fares and courier shift so their difficulty and timers are tuned for humans rather than script-teleported cars
